svg.text: Burger Factory Simulation - Clean UML Overview
Complete class structure, organized for presentation: MVC, Model composition, Machine inheritance, value types, and relationship summary
main.cpp creates BurgerFactoryModel, FactoryController, and FactoryView. Each frame: controller.update(dt), then view.render().

g.text: owns concrete stations through Machine abstraction

svg.text: BurgerFactoryModel coordinates the process, while managers own detailed responsibilities.
InventoryManager = ingredients, MoneyManager = money, OrderManager = orders, ProductionLine = machines.
View depends only on IFactoryViewData. Controller depends only on IFactoryActions.

g.text: BurgerFactoryModel uses ProcessStep, IngredientType, MachineConfig, BurgerRecipe, BurgerType, Order.
ProductionLine uses ProcessStep, MachineConfig, BurgerRecipe, IngredientType, and QualityChecker.
Machine has state: MachineState. Order and MachineConfig depend on BurgerType.
BurgerRecipe depends on BurgerType and IngredientType. InventoryManager uses IngredientType.
Every station can be treated as a Machine and override update(dt).
The model coordinates inventory, money, orders, and production line objects.
ProductionLine owns stations through unique_ptr<Machine> for polymorphism.
View depends on IFactoryViewData; Controller depends on IFactoryActions.
BurgerFactoryModel asks ProductionLine, and QualityChecker performs inspect().
New machines extend Machine. UI changes stay in View. Money, order, inventory,
and quality logic are separated into focused classes.
